qualifying_findings.title: Anthropic reports disrupted Claude misuse across cyber, surveillance, influence, conventional-weapons, biological, fraud, and distillation cases
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Anthropic's September 2026 threat-intelligence report says its team identified and disrupted Claude misuse from December 2025 through August 2026 across seven harm areas. The report describes AI-augmented cyber operations, including Russian-state-nexus activity consistent with Midnight Blizzard, AI-driven phishing, credential theft, malware evasion loops, data exfiltration, and compromised hotel WiFi/DNS hijacking. It also describes Russian developers using Claude for autonomous drone software, biological-misuse attempts, surveillance systems, influence operations, scams, and illicit distillation.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: Primary public threat report added case studies, IOCs, affected threat boundaries, disrupted activity, and safeguards/partner-sharing claims.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary threat-intelligence report with reputable public reporting corroboration
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Claude Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus were used in cases covered by the report; Anthropic states Claude Fable and Mythos were not involved except for one illicit distillation case.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The report gives concrete evidence that AI tools are used not only as assistants but as orchestration layers across reconnaissance, exploitation, exfiltration, malware retooling, surveillance, and weapons-related software tasks.

qualifying_findings.title: OmniRoute ACP custom-agent endpoint allows remote code execution through attacker-controlled interpreter arguments
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: OmniRoute 3.8.49 and earlier accepted attacker-controlled binary and versionCommand values at POST /api/acp/agents and reached an execFileSync sink after only limited filtering and a self-consistency check. The advisory states anonymous exploitation was possible when requireLogin=false or during a fresh-instance bootstrap window; otherwise exploitation required a management session or management-scoped API key. No fixed version was available as of the advisory review.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: New/updated public CVE record for critical remote code execution in an AI gateway custom-agent endpoint.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services record plus NVD enrichment and GitHub advisory links
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OmniRoute <= 3.8.49; no fixed version available as of advisory review.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI gateways mediate model-provider access and agent endpoints; command execution in a gateway container can expose credentials, traffic, model-routing controls, and downstream integrations.

qualifying_findings.title: knowns MCP code.find tool permits path traversal outside the project root
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: knowns through 0.33.0 fails to restrict the path argument of the code.find MCP tool to the project root. The record says an attacker can supply absolute paths or traversal sequences and retrieve full file contents outside the intended project directory.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: In-window CVE update for MCP tool path traversal with proof-of-concept exploitation noted in CISA ADP enrichment.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services record, VulnCheck advisory, and GitHub advisory references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP tools that read project files are delegated-authority boundaries; path traversal turns a project-scoped read tool into a host-level disclosure path for AI agent sessions.

qualifying_findings.title: IBM Langflow OSS receives multiple code-execution and MCP endpoint CVEs
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD returned 15 Langflow records in the in-window query. Sampled direct CVE records describe IBM Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.11.5 vulnerabilities including unauthenticated code execution and chat-session access via publicly shared MCP project endpoints, static security scanner bypass leading to OS command execution, incomplete denylist code execution, improper validation of MCP stdio command-line arguments, and bypass of server-side controls intended to block local subprocess transport through MCP Tools components.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: Multiple public CVE records for Langflow code-execution, session-isolation, scanner-bypass, and MCP subprocess controls were published or updated in the window.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: IBM PSIRT-sourced CVE records via CVE Services and NVD
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Langflow is an LLM application builder; public-flow MCP endpoints, custom-component scanners, and MCP stdio subprocess configuration are core AI application security boundaries.

qualifying_findings.factual_summary: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway 1.0.0 through 1.0.7 could allow a remote attacker to gain administrative access because of default credentials. NVD reports a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8 and CISA ADP marks the issue automatable with total technical impact.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: In-window CVE publication/update for default-credential administrative access in an MCP gateway.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: IBM PSIRT-sourced CVE record via CVE Services and NVD
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP gateways concentrate delegated tool access, identity, and audit controls; default admin credentials compromise the mediator rather than a single downstream tool.

qualifying_findings.title: Flowise node-load-method allows cross-workspace credential IDOR and confused-deputy provider calls
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Flowise up to and including 3.1.3 exposes POST /api/v1/node-load-method/:name without route-level permission checks and decrypts credentials by raw Credential.id without verifying workspace ownership. A low-privilege user or workspace API key in one workspace can supply another workspace's credential ID and make Flowise perform provider calls, including Google Drive, Google Sheets, and AWS DynamoDB metadata calls, using victim credentials. The raw secret is not returned. The issue is fixed in Flowise 3.1.4.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: New public CVE for cross-workspace credential authorization failure in an LLM application builder.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services record and VulnCheck advisory with GitHub advisory reference
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Flowise credentials connect AI workflows to external data providers; cross-workspace confused-deputy calls break tenant isolation and least-privilege boundaries for AI tool integrations.

qualifying_findings.factual_summary: WPBot before 8.5.7 lacks authorization or nonce checks on several AJAX actions that relay prompts to configured AI providers. Unauthenticated attackers can make third-party AI provider API calls using the site's configured API keys and consume associated cost.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: New public CVE for unauthenticated AI provider API abuse in a WordPress chatbot plugin.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: WPScan CVE Services record with NVD enrichment
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The issue turns site-owned AI provider credentials into an unauthenticated spend and API-abuse surface, directly implicating credential scoping and cost-control boundaries.

qualifying_findings.title: WPBot chat-session listing exposes visitor contact data without authorization
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD reports that WPBot before 8.6.0 lacks capability or nonce checks on the AJAX action that lists stored chat sessions. Unauthenticated attackers can retrieve the name, email address, and phone number of every chat visitor by requesting a wide date range.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: New public NVD record for unauthenticated disclosure of chatbot visitor personal data.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Chatbots often collect support, sales, or identity context; unauthenticated session export exposes AI interaction metadata and visitor PII.

qualifying_findings.title: n8n Instance AI vulnerabilities receive in-window NVD updates
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD updated two n8n Instance AI records inside the window. CVE-2026-86074 describes a credential setup flow that accepted a fetched credential test or verification URL without ensuring it matched the workflow node origin, enabling attacker-controlled content to influence authenticated requests, redirects, or probes to another origin. CVE-2026-86078 describes prototype pollution in Instance AI workflow summaries where submitted workflow node names and connection keys could write to Object.prototype and disrupt later requests. Both are fixed in n8n 2.37.7 and 2.38.2.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: Official NVD enrichment/analysis changed inside the window for two AI workflow automation vulnerabilities.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD records plus direct CVE Services and GitHub advisory references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Instance AI bridges workflow-generated content, credential testing, and workflow summarization; the records touch origin validation, SSRF-like probing, prototype pollution, and availability of AI-enabled automation services.

qualifying_findings.title: Flowise CSV Agent prompt-injection RCE receives in-window NVD update
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD's prompt query returned an in-window update for CVE-2026-70477. The record describes Flowise before 3.1.3, where prompt injection against a chatflow using the CSV Agent node can make the LLM produce malicious Python that bypasses a blocklist validator and executes in an unsandboxed Pyodide environment. NVD reports CVSS 3.1 9.8 critical and points to the Flowise 3.1.3 fix.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_delta: In-window NVD update for an existing critical prompt-injection-to-code-execution record.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD record with GitHub advisory, commit, pull request, and release-note references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a direct example of prompt injection crossing into executable code in an AI application builder, showing why generated-code execution needs sandbox and validator controls.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence for current-window novelty: the vulnerability itself was published on 2026-08-04, so only the NVD update qualifies for this run. It may already have been captured in earlier collector output.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, deduplicate against existing Flowise prompt-injection records.
If already synthesized, treat this as an NVD enrichment update rather than a new incident.
